critical_steps: The diagonal scalar condition extends from a dense subset by continuity.
For a real Hilbert space, vanishing diagonal values force only the symmetric part of the defect operator to vanish.
The explicit mixed operator is \(I+J\) with nonzero skew-adjoint \(J\), while its symmetric part is \(I\).
The two displayed sequences are Riesz bases and satisfy the scalar condition exactly.
Every bounded skew-adjoint defect is realizable by taking \(g_j=(I-J)e_j\).
integrity.proof_basis: Real polarization plus an exact two-dimensional Riesz-basis counterexample.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made that the source's complex-Hilbert characterization fails or that the classical real-polarization lemma is new.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects only the real-Hilbert scalar characterization in Remark 1.2; the complex-Hilbert branch is not challenged.
Real polarization is classical operator theory and is used as prior input; the source-specific characterization and frame realization are the accepted claim.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal author correction may contain the same observation.
title: A real quadratic-form test sees only the symmetric part of a \(K\)-dual operator
